subject.title: #282 A: add trusted gateway context contract

question: Should OpenClaw establish a public plugin contract that exposes full inbound identity and raw message content, or keep trusted provenance internal and provide a narrower capability-scoped action context?
rationale: The answer determines a durable plugin API, third-party plugin data-access scope, and the correct queue aggregation model; automation cannot safely choose those trust and privacy boundaries.

options.title: Narrow host-owned contract
options.body: Keep construction internal, make the value readonly or opaque, preserve per-message queue provenance, and expose only approved action fields to the consuming plugin boundary.

options.title: Approve broad plugin context
options.body: Explicitly treat installed plugins as entitled to full inbound raw text and identity, document that contract, and define how batched messages map to context values.

options.title: Pause the core API
options.body: Use existing narrow fields such as requesterSenderId and implement the attendance workflow externally until a concrete missing core seam is demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Narrow host-owned contract
recommendation.body: Keep construction internal, make the value readonly or opaque, preserve per-message queue provenance, and expose only approved action fields to the consuming plugin boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history spans the plugin SDK, hook contexts, and reply/runtime boundaries involved in this decision.
